title: Proof-Carrying Materials: Falsifiable Safety Certificates for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: arXiv:2603.12183v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are deployed for high-throughput materials screening without formal reliability guarantees. We show that a single MLIP used as a stability filter misses 93% of density functional theory (DFT)-stable materials (recall 0.07) on a 25,000-material benchmark. Proof-Carrying Materials (PCM) closes this gap through three stages: adversarial falsification across compositional space, bootstrap envelope refinement with 95% confidence intervals, and Lean 4 formal certification. Auditing CHGNet, TensorNet and MACE reveals architecture-specific blind spots with near-zero pairwise error correlations (r <= 0.13; n = 5,000), confirmed by independent Quantum ESPRESSO validation (20/20 converged; median DFT/CHGNet force ratio 12x). tldr: 提出证明携带材料（PCM）框架，通过对抗性证伪、自助包络细化和Lean 4形式化认证三个阶段，为机器学习原子间势提供可证伪的安全证书，解决了单一MLIP作为稳定性过滤器会漏掉93% DFT稳定材料的可靠性问题。
en_tdlr: Proposes Proof-Carrying Materials (PCM), a three-stage framework combining adversarial falsification, bootstrap envelope refinement, and Lean 4 formal certification to provide falsifiable safety certificates for machine-learned interatomic potentials, addressing the problem that a single MLIP stability filter misses 93% of DFT-stable materials.
